sentences.en: Daniel, last week we published our long-awaited updated Tesla valuation.
You can find it on the ark-invest site.
Many of our readers were waiting for this since our 2029 valuation.
This is our 2031 valuation.
There's a few important things that are updated about this model, but you know, let's talk about the headline figures.
First, the majority of Tesla's value we believe in the next 5 years will be attributable to robotaxi.
So, that that's a that's a constant as we had you know, in the in the previous model.
That number went down slightly.

It's roughly 80% of the enterprise value we think in 2021 will be attributable to robotaxi, and that's because in the time period we expect Optima Optimus to scale incrementally more than we assumed would happen 2 years prior.
Yeah, that's exactly right.

So, our last model, the 2029, had the robotaxi really at roughly 90% as you say, and the decline towards the 80% is because of the one of the main updates we made this year was external Optimus sales.
So, for context, by 2031, our base case assumes that there will be roughly 1 million Optimus deployed earning robot as a service revenue with software as a service like margins.
And for context for the viewers of 1 million deployed by 2031, that is very conservative relative to Elon's statements.
So, for the same year in 2031, Elon is on the record of saying he believes there could be 100 million or 1 billion Optimus deployed.
So, relative to our 1 million base case, it's quite conservative there, and that was one of the main updates along with various other ones, which is really driving some of the price changes.
And to you know, quickly do a pit stop on Optimus.

So, so last time we published our 2029 price target, you know, it seemed like we actually got some feedback from Elon based on his public comments that you know, he thought we were too conservative on our on our
Optimus figures.
So they have increased of course, you know, Daniel as you mentioned, nowhere near some of the you know, estimates that we've heard could be could be possible in the time period.

But I'll also say that I feel like on the on the earnings calls, you know, we just had a recent Tesla earnings call, they've become incrementally maybe it's just sort of shaping the opinions that they see out there,

But they have sort of cautioned, you know, "Hey, this is actually quite a hard manufacturing pro- problem, you know, it's not just a data problem, although that's an another thing to tackle here to get the training data to
Make Optimus work well.
But actually, you know, the manufacturing, getting the robot right, the hands are still very difficult.
There's sort of a lot of upfront challenges here in the near term to get this thing really off the ground.
But they do expect it to ship to customers end of next year.
So we assume they must have you know, minimum viable product in order to do that, minimum functionality that customers will accept.

Yeah, and I think you said this before, Tasha, and I think it's a really interesting point relative to the robo-taxi opportunity, a manually driven robot or a car is a lot more functional than a manually operated Optimus.

So on the on your data point, it's kind of Tesla needs to bootstrap the data and hence why they're talking about the Optimus Academy which they mentioned on the earnings call for a second time of 10 to 20
To 30,000 robots to train.
But to your point too, even before that, it sounds like there are a number of hardware changes and developments that are needed really to start gathering that data.
Right.
Right.
It's tough to sell you know, a dumb, so to speak, robot to customers before the functionality is there.
And as you said, they talked about you know, they think they need just 10 to 20,000 in order to self-play or sort of learn from action, which makes sense.
And you know, Tesla's pretty well set up, to do that training exercise, and they have, you know, an in-house manufacturing facility to train the robots on.
We know that the first applications of them are going to be industrial use cases or manufacturing use cases.
So, you know, still very well positioned as a vertically integrated player here, but, you know, the fact of the matter is it's still early in this market.
Yeah, exactly.
And then maybe to talk about Tesla another area of the model that I updated, and it actually relates to Optimus, is the idea of AI infrastructure and compute.
Since we published our model two years ago, everyone is talking about GPUs for training, for inference.

So, to account for that, we added a new line to the model on AI infrastructure, and really how it's modeled is that as Tesla spends more dollars on their AI infrastructure, the capability of Optimus grows.
To your point on functionality and tasks that it can complete.
So, included in our blog, to put some numbers to it, we estimate that by 2031, Tesla could cumulatively spend on average at 225 billion dollars on AI infrastructure.
That's really across chips, the Terafab initiative, and other line items that feed into that.
And that's up from roughly 7 billion at the end of last year.
So, quite a large ramp up, but as we're seeing across all of the AI hyperscalers, the conversations are really going into the trillions out from the billions.
So, that was another meaningful update that is part of our model this year.
Yes, and that, you know, begs the question, what do we have to say about the merger?
We are going to get to that.
I'm going to tease that.
We will we will talk about the merger.
Right now, you know, our Tesla evaluation values it as a standalone business, but we do have thoughts on the merger.
But, before we get there, we should also talk about robotaxis.
Of course, you know, the biggest part of the model here.
An update that we made in the on the robotaxi piece of business is we updated the pricing that we think is possible for robotaxis.
This is based on some research that looks at customer willingness to pay across income deciles or income levels.
And basically the end result is we think that you know, there is more of an appetite for slightly higher prices at various segments in the market.
You know, at or above ride-hail prices today.
So basically you know, if you look at the average price of ride-hail today, it's $2.80.
One of the reasons that we think that autonomous ride-hail could proliferate, $2.80 per mile I should say.

One of the one of the reasons we think autonomous ride-hail could proliferate is because you know, at scale and at scale when there's with this is a you know, there are many more vehicles on the road than we
See today.
It's more prolific in cities.
It's really you know, a meaningful option compared to human-driven ride-hail.
So at that point you can you can undercut ride-hail with an autonomous car because it's inherently cheaper to operate.
And we think utilization rate could actually be better than human-driven vehicles.
So that's what's really going to expand the market.
Those lower prices, but you know, you don't necessarily have to start at those lower prices, right?
They we know that in metro areas there's many people that will be willing to pay higher prices.
We see that in ride-hail today.
And in fact, you know, one conservative part of the model is that we're not assuming you know, any surge pricing here.
And we know that people that are at the you know, highest income deciles actually end up traveling the most.
And it's during peak hours.
So there is certainly more room for that than I think that we provide in the current analysis.
We're conservative there.
So just one area of potential upside.
But that had a meaningful impact as well and on our price target.
Yeah, and as you say conservatism Tasha, it reminds me we often get asked about FSD and the monthly subscription payment.
And really another area of conservatism, but really it's because of we think that the size of the opportunity is that we currently don't model for FSD subscription.
That said, the latest earnings call, they gave a lot of information on how adoption is.

I think they said that roughly 75% of North American deliveries included a full self-driving subscription, and that's extremely notable because you receive 1 month free regardless, but people are still paying ahead of that 1 month.
So, really showing that now FSD is the product, and the car is the means of delivering that.
But, that's an area that isn't included in the model really because of the size that of the robo taxi opportunity that you just described, Tasha.
Right.
But, you know, could be potentially meaningful in the near term.
You know, we heard Pierre Ferragu on the call say that he he's estimating it's roughly, you know, getting a close to a billion in ARR, and they confirmed that estimate.
So, certainly could be meaningful in the near term.
And yeah, the 75% attach rate, we've done some analysis on that suggests if you just look at that, you know, that's improved since the last quarter by 20 points.

It's very good if you look at let's say like Sirius XM or other subscriptions that you have in cars, GM Super Cruise, products that are cheaper and actually offered longer trial periods than just a month.
The you know, the 75% would, you know, beat both of those handily.
And if you just look at it on average SAS pricing as well, it looks pretty good.
Again, just using the most recent quarterly point.
Okay.
I've teased it enough.
We have to talk about the merger.
So, you know, we get asked this question a lot.
So, one I think I think we'll start with you know, from our perspective, the merger is beneficial for both companies.
Why?
Well, from both of their perspectives, you know, the Terafab is meant to alleviate chip constraints.
If Elon's estimates for Optimus are, you know, anywhere close to what Tesla produces in the next 5 to 10 years, they're going to need a lot of chips.
So, Tesla can work with Basic to do that.
I you know, it can alleviate some sort of stress on management bandwidth, which I don't think should be overlooked.
Especially for a project that important, but also across both companies.
We know Elon spends a lot of time at both companies.
And you know, we've also heard Elon say that from the for large-scale deployments of Optimus, that you can have the SpaceX AI or SpaceX SI models as the orchestration layer here for Optimus.
So we know that they'll mutually benefit from each other.
And I'm missing a couple points, Daniel.
What are they?
Yeah, so if you look at what Elon's concerned about today, Tasha you touched on chips through Terafab, and then the other one really is power.
So SpaceX and Tesla respectively are aiming for 100 gigawatts in annual solar capacity, which is roughly five to six times more than what the US produced last year.
So that's another area of convergence.
And then maybe one other point is the Cybertrucks we now know are starting to roll out with Starlink connectivity for media consumption when you're enjoying your driverless robotaxis.
So there's a lot of areas pointing to the synergies related to potential SpaceX Tesla merger.
So And the last the last one we should we should also we'd be remiss if we didn't mention that we think the robotaxi business, as we've laid out in our model, will be very cash flow generative.
Yes.

Totally changing Tesla's business model from selling vehicles and getting some subscription revenue to really a recurring revenue business with which we think will have quite attractive margins, could push Tesla's gross margins close to 70% as a whole by
2031 the autonomous ride-hail business.
So again, that'll be useful for funding the AI ambitions of SpaceX or really the combined entity, as you'd have it.
Yeah, exactly.
Yeah.
And I mean SpaceX has kind of done that playbook before with Starlink, but to your point, robotaxis is kind of like Starlink on steroids as it relates to cash flow generative ability.
So yeah, it seems like a lot of signs are pointing that way.
Yes, but we you know, we did hear again a little bit of conservatism on the on the SpaceX call around the merger.
You know, it's we Elon said this is it's not we you cannot assume it's a certainty.
Of course, they need over 50% of all shares at Tesla to agree to this all shareholders.
So, you know, we'll see that's a high hurdle to clear.
Again, we see that there's definitely benefit.
It looks like you know, it seems like the management team supports this as well.
But sort of the timing of when exactly this will happen, it does look like it's near term, but you can't pinpoint the date exactly.
Within the next in the next 5 years, likely sooner, but we'll see.
We don't we don't have any special information there.
And you know, exactly what the price is, we've seen estimates of you know, a 30% 50% premium.
We'll see where that shakes out.
But you know, I think again the benefit of the combination to us is clear.
Yeah, and included in our Tesla valuation, as you mentioned Tasha, we measured it as a standalone business, but there's a portion on what the business could look like in 2031 should it converge.
So, we'd encourage everyone to look at that potential breakdown to get an idea of what the future could hold for a combined SpaceX Tesla entity.
Right.

And I and I think the story is there that you know, near term it may look like SpaceX is the big beneficiary here you know, getting Tesla's cash, but long term you know, we actually think that SpaceX with
Its AI business growing exponentially as it is today could be you know, the majority of revenue and earnings for the combined entity.
So long term you know, Tesla will benefit from that.
So, again, mutual benefit for both companies and picture will certainly change dramatically the AI build out over the next 5 years.
Absolutely.

So, we touched on a lot of things Tesla today, Tasha, with our new model as well as SpaceX and really for everyone to stay up-to-date, I would encourage you to go to ark-invest.com, look out for our Tesla model,
And also follow us on all social media platforms.

For myself and Tasha, it's X @DimaGuarArk and @TashaArk, where we post regular updates on all things Tesla, SpaceX, and really the converging world we live in with all of the great technologies we're following.

vocab.usage: the combined entity 合併後的實體；a legal entity 法律實體
vocab.example: The combined entity could fund SpaceX's AI ambitions.
vocab.example_zh: 合併後的實體可以用來資助 SpaceX 的 AI 計畫。

vocab.usage: a meaningful update 重大更新；meaningful change 有意義的改變
vocab.example: That was another meaningful update to our model this year.
vocab.example_zh: 那是我們今年模型裡又一個重大更新。

vocab.usage: how adoption is 採用情況如何；user adoption 使用者採用率
vocab.example: The earnings call gave a lot of information on adoption.
vocab.example_zh: 法說會提供了很多關於採用情況的資訊。

vocab.usage: what a company produces 公司生產的數量；produce robots 生產機器人
vocab.example: If Tesla produces that many Optimus robots, they will need a lot of chips.
vocab.example_zh: 如果特斯拉生產那麼多 Optimus，就會需要大量晶片。

vocab.usage: social media platforms 社群平台；a software platform 軟體平台
vocab.example: Follow us on all social media platforms.
vocab.example_zh: 請在各個社群平台追蹤我們。

vocab.usage: pointing to 指向／顯示出；point to synergies 顯示有綜效
vocab.example: There are a lot of areas pointing to the synergies.
vocab.example_zh: 有很多跡象顯示雙方有綜效。

vocab.zh: 估值；評估（此處口語／字幕多半指 valuation 估值）
vocab.usage: a Tesla evaluation 特斯拉估值；an evaluation of… 對…的評估
vocab.example: Our Tesla evaluation still values it as a standalone business.
vocab.example_zh: 我們對特斯拉的估值仍把它視為獨立事業。

vocab.usage: for the viewers 給觀眾的說明；TV viewers 電視觀眾
vocab.example: For the viewers, that figure is very conservative.
vocab.example_zh: 跟觀眾說明一下，那個數字其實非常保守。

vocab.usage: it reminds me 這讓我想起；remind someone of… 使某人想起
vocab.example: It reminds me we often get asked about FSD.
vocab.example_zh: 這讓我想起，我們常常被問到 FSD。

vocab.usage: hardware developments 硬體上的進展；new developments 新進展
vocab.example: A number of hardware developments are still needed.
vocab.example_zh: 還需要不少硬體上的進展。

vocab.usage: inherently cheaper 本質上更便宜；cheaper to operate 營運成本更低
vocab.example: An autonomous car is inherently cheaper to operate.
vocab.example_zh: 自駕車的營運成本本質上更低。

vocab.usage: earning revenue 賺取收入；earn a margin 賺取利潤
vocab.example: The robots will be earning robot-as-a-service revenue.
vocab.example_zh: 這些機器人將賺取機器人即服務的收入。

vocab.usage: not assuming any… 並沒有假設任何…；assuming that 假設
vocab.example: We are not assuming any surge pricing in the model.
vocab.example_zh: 模型裡我們並沒有假設會有尖峰加價。

vocab.usage: likely sooner 可能還會更早；sooner than expected 比預期更早
vocab.example: It will happen within five years, likely sooner.
vocab.example_zh: 這會在五年內發生，可能還更早。

vocab.usage: gather data 蒐集資料；start gathering 開始蒐集
vocab.example: They still need hardware changes to start gathering that data.
vocab.example_zh: 他們還需要改硬體，才能開始蒐集那些資料。

vocab.usage: mutual benefit 互利；mutual interest 共同利益
vocab.example: It is a mutual benefit for both companies.
vocab.example_zh: 這對兩家公司都有好處。

vocab.usage: end up traveling 結果出行很多；travel the most 出行最多
vocab.example: People in the highest income deciles end up traveling the most.
vocab.example_zh: 收入最高的那一群人，出行其實最多。

vocab.usage: an earnings call 法說會；latest earnings 最新財報
vocab.example: The latest earnings call gave a lot of information.
vocab.example_zh: 最近一次法說會提供了很多資訊。

vocab.usage: the timing of… …的時機；near-term timing 近期時點
vocab.example: The timing of when exactly this will happen is still unclear.
vocab.example_zh: 這件事究竟何時發生，時點仍不清楚。

vocab.usage: vertically integrated 垂直整合的；an integrated player 整合業者
vocab.example: Tesla is still well positioned as a vertically integrated player.
vocab.example_zh: 特斯拉作為垂直整合業者，位置仍然很好。

vocab.usage: we estimate that 我們估計；estimate spending 估計支出
vocab.example: We estimate that Tesla could spend $225 billion on AI infrastructure.
vocab.example_zh: 我們估計特斯拉可能會在 AI 基礎建設上投入 2,250 億美元。

vocab.usage: touch on 提到；you touched on 你剛才提到
vocab.example: You touched on chips, and the other issue is power.
vocab.example_zh: 你提到了晶片，另一個問題則是電力。

vocab.usage: hardware changes 硬體變更；hardware and software 硬體與軟體
vocab.example: Hardware changes are needed to start gathering that data.
vocab.example_zh: 要開始蒐集那些資料，還需要改硬體。

vocab.usage: Elon's estimates 馬斯克的估計；close to the estimates 接近那些估計
vocab.example: If Elon's estimates for Optimus are close, they will need a lot of chips.
vocab.example_zh: 如果馬斯克對 Optimus 的估計差不多準，他們會需要大量晶片。

vocab.usage: the conversations are going into… 討論已經進入…；have conversations 進行討論
vocab.example: The conversations are really going into the trillions.
vocab.example_zh: 這些討論的規模已經進入兆美元等級。
